probe: pinned /api/data-maid report, finalize, view and delete (JSON report + in-memory token over absolute paths)

conventions.orderedSteps: steps is an ARRAY and MUST be replayed in order: every step shares one user tree and one token store, so a keyed map would desynchronise every later snapshot while still passing
conventions.tokens: the token is 32 random bytes and is never recorded: requests carry a <token:STEP> reference, the report body carries <token>, and the CONSEQUENCES are asserted (what it unlocks, what an unknown/consumed cross-handle token answers, that a 400 does not consume it)
conventions.hashes: each record hash is sha256 of an ABSOLUTE path, so the fixture records <hash:CATEGORY:IDENTITY> and the replay substitutes its own hash for the same identity. The hash RULE is a labelled source-derived assertion in the replay.
conventions.reportArrays: report arrays are sorted by (parent, name) before recording because pinned emits directory enumeration order; report content-length and ETag are therefore shape-classified and not recorded
conventions.tree: the whole user root after every step, with / paths, sorted, excluding stats.json (pinned startup writes the boot wall-clock timestamp there, not this domain)
conventions.outbound: this domain never leaves the process; every step asserts 0 outbound requests, and the pinned server boots under the shared egress stub (node-fetch AND global fetch replaced)
conventions.mtime: seeded files carry a whole-second mtime (utimes 1700000000), so mtime is the same integer on every host

steps.name: report.seeded
steps.description: mints a token over the seeded tree; every collector reports its loose files and not the referenced ones

shapeReason.headers.content-length: content-length measures the report body, whose array order is directory enumeration order (NTFS != ext4); the fixture records the arrays sorted
shapeReason.headers.etag: the ETag is a digest of the report body and therefore of the enumeration order, which is host-dependent
shapeReason.bodyBase64: the report body cannot be recorded verbatim: it carries the random token and one sha256 of an absolute path per record
shapeReason.bodySha256: a digest of the verbatim report body, which contains the token and absolute-path hashes
shapeReason.bodyLength: the length of the verbatim report body, which is only meaningful with the unsorted arrays

steps.name: view.looseImage
steps.description: the token addresses a file by hash and the bytes come back with the mime-types type

steps.name: view.unknownExtension
steps.description: a known mime type (.bin) is served as application/octet-stream, not as text/plain

steps.name: view.chatJsonl
steps.description: mime-types has no .jsonl entry, so the pinned `|| text/plain` fallback answers without a charset

steps.name: view.unknownHash
steps.description: a hash the token does not cover is 404, which is distinct from the 403 of a bad token

steps.name: view.missingQuery
steps.description: neither query member present is 400, before any token lookup

steps.name: view.emptyToken
steps.description: an empty token is falsy in JS, so this is 400 rather than the 403 of an unknown token

steps.name: view.duplicateToken
steps.description: Express turns a repeated query key into an array, and the pinned `.toString()` joins it with "," — so the token no longer matches: 403

steps.name: view.duplicateHash
steps.description: the same join on the hash reaches the token and then misses the path list: 404, which is the 403/404 split between token and hash

steps.name: view.unknownToken
steps.description: an unknown token is 403, and the hash being real changes nothing

steps.name: finalize.missingToken
steps.description: a body without a token is 400

steps.name: view.afterFailedFinalize
steps.description: a rejected finalize does not consume the token: the same view still answers 200

steps.name: finalize.unknownToken
steps.description: an unknown token is 403

steps.name: finalize.ok
steps.description: 204 with the pinned 204 framing (no content-type or length, ETag of "No Content")

steps.name: view.afterFinalize
steps.description: finalize really removed the token: the same view is now 403

steps.name: delete.afterFinalize
steps.description: delete with a consumed token is 403 and removes nothing

steps.name: report.second
steps.description: a second report; the consumed token is gone and this one replaces it

steps.name: delete.missingHashes
steps.description: the shape guard (400) runs before the token lookup

steps.name: delete.hashesNotArray
steps.description: a non-array hashes member is 400

steps.name: delete.emptyHashes
steps.description: an empty hashes array is 400

steps.name: delete.unknownHashSkipped
steps.description: a hash the token does not cover is silently skipped and the answer is still 204

steps.name: delete.ok
steps.description: 204 and the tree loses exactly that one file

steps.name: view.deletedFile
steps.description: the token still lists the path but the file is gone: 404, not 500

steps.name: report.afterDelete
steps.description: the deleted image no longer appears in a fresh report

steps.name: view.guestCannotUseToken
steps.description: a token belongs to the handle that minted it: the guest-user session gets 403

steps.name: finalize.guestCannotUseToken
steps.description: the same gate on finalize, so a borrow attempt cannot destroy the owner's token

steps.name: delete.guestCannotUseToken
steps.description: and on delete, the destructive route: 403 and nothing removed
